notes: Loop-1 refine landed in the product: who did what, an AI take-home, result entry and calendar dates in /try, the 2027 wage demo and an honest 'not yet'. The loop-3 personas now point to one pattern: the owner's own voice is thin where it matters. On /try, What-IF sets her range, her switching share and any blank cost (Selin, educator). The AI lesson rests on a comparison of two different casts (hackathon, Selin), and /try, the beta's main path, has no AI in it at all. No real owner has used it: 0 of 10 cafés (hackathon). So: make the guesses hers and calibrate them, make the AI lesson a fair experiment, and start the beta as a measured test.
improvements: 1. What: Make every guess that moves the money the owner's own, and turn the test into calibration. /try asks her bad-day and good-day numbers and how many of 10 lunch regulars would switch, and it makes 'fällt nicht an' a choice. After the test, What-IF shows which of her guesses missed, and by how much, and starts the next test from what she counted. Why: Selin's first finding: a blank 'Was kostet Sie der Test?' became 0 € and a '+266 € macht Gewinn' headline (product.selin.json; try-report.txt:67). The educator found that '/try sets the range itself' and that the owner never states her own uncertainty, and after the test asks to 'explain the miss guess by guess' with a next-test button (product.educator.json, improvements 3 and 5). The visual reviewer asks for the same stand-in warning (visual.json, improvement 3). It serves vision core step 6 and the landing's own promise 'damit Ihre nächste Schätzung besser wird' (landing.txt:165), and the transferable decision lesson the hackathon judge scores. It is also an AI lesson: a number a tool fills in is a guess someone else made for you. Smallest version: two /try screens, 'An einem schlechten / guten Tag: wie viele zusätzliche?' and 'Von 10 Mittagsstammgästen: wie viele würden wechseln?', each with 'Weiß ich nicht'. Add a 'Fällt nicht an' button per cost and a stand-in line above the short answer. On the result page, add one attribution line ('2 Gäste weniger: −107 €; 21 % statt 30 % Wechsel: +41 €') and a 'Nächster Test' button that prefills /try with her counts. Risk: two more screens between customers, so keep 'Weiß ich nicht' to one tap and fold the review page. Attribution can look precise, so label it as calculated from her counts and her guesses. Never call it forecast accuracy, and never score the owner.

2. What: Teach AI through two fair, visible contrasts instead of sentences. First, the same six imagined guests, played once by fixed rules and once by Claude, side by side with the brief Claude got. Second, public rules as a fifth kind of number that carries a date ('Öffentliche Regel · Stand 1. Januar 2026'). Why: the hackathon judge's weakest point has moved from 'AI invisible' to comparability: 'two different casts cannot show that Wer die Gäste spielt, verändert die Geschichte'. The judge also notes that the AI's words sit behind taps and that the take-home names only four kinds of number (product.hackathon.json, improvements 1, 2 and 4). Selin followed 'Denselben Probelauf' to six different names (product.selin.json). The educator found 'Fakt' used both for her till numbers and for public rules (product.educator.json, improvement 4). On /try, the beta's main path, the owner meets no AI at all ('Von einer KI: nichts', try-report.txt:48), so these contrasts are her AI lesson. Smallest version: run the fixed rules on demo-ai.json's cast and event, and show one row: 'Dieselben 6 Gäste: feste Regeln x probiert · Claude 3 probiert, 0 erzählt'. Open two Claude answers, with the brief beside one ('Das wusste Claude nicht: Ihre Kosten, Ihre Gewinnschwelle'), and link this from a /try report after its rule-based run. Add the rule chip and the line 'Was eine KI über Steuern oder Löhne weiß, hat ein Datum' to the take-home, in all four languages. Risk: Claude's fluent answers can look more credible than the rules, so keep 'Ausgedacht' on both and say that neither is data. A fifth label adds load, so reserve 'Fakt' for public rules only.

3. What: Start the Berlin beta as a measured test of What-IF itself. That means a permanent link, the first 10 invite cards, at least 3 cafés on /try alone, and an opt-in 'Ergebnis an What-IF schicken' button that sends her result link to the beta contact only if she taps it. Why: the hackathon judge marks proof of use 'not fixed' and asks for one dated session note (product.hackathon.json, improvement 5). vision.md calls a short test with a real owner stronger proof than a feature list, and it measures progress by whether owners explain the assumptions, try the test and come back. PRD 12.5 wrote those measures down, and every one stands at 0 of 10. Selin says she would run the test, but only because she filled in Frage 9 herself. The /try-alone cafés will show whether owners without a helper fall into the silent-zero trap. Smallest version: deploy to a permanent https URL (the pitch runs on a quick tunnel, docs/09-pitch-videos.md:46) and print three German invite cards. Run two 30-minute sessions on owners' phones with their Z-reports, and give one café /try alone. Write consented, dated notes with the fields the PRD defines, and add the opt-in mailto button under 'Wie geht es weiter?'. Risk: founder-led sessions inflate understanding, so note who helped. Three cafés prove nothing statistical, so report counts ('2 von 3'), never percentages, and never a benchmark across cafés. A report link carries her numbers, so it goes only where she sends it, and nothing is collected silently.
